checks.topic: Detailed-event omission is logging-only and remains a prefix
checks.detail: Once an event would exceed 768KiB including separator allowance or the actual token budget, events_omitted increments and record returns Ok. Every later detail is omitted. Scheduling, native host calls, configured step/wait checks, live-mouse limits and cooperative cancellation are unchanged.

checks.topic: Real errors, cancellation, partial effects and cleanup
checks.detail: cleanup_attempted increments before host.close; cleanup_failed increments from its result before logging. Counts survive omitted close records. execute_on still combines execution and cleanup errors, reports failed for either and retains both error strings when both fail. No rollback or accepted-by-application claim is introduced; omission is explicit and does not justify replay.

checks.topic: Actual parser token accounting and final framing reserve
checks.detail: token_count uses the same Document parser and tokens_used. Detailed events are capped at65536-256=65280 tokens. Current receipt adds31 tokens outside events; modern text-only MCP adds27 more. Maximum65338 leaves198 tokens below65536. Existing event layouts contain fixed members; dynamic target strings are escaped and do not add JSON members.

checks.topic: Exact encoded capacity retry cannot replay actions
checks.detail: The result and is_error already exist before encode. The closure only invokes protocol.tool_result with the same content/structured value. Only Buffer with needed>current length triggers one resize and one retry. Writer continues counting all raw/escaped segments after insufficient space and returns exact needed; no Runtime, script execution or outer handle is reinvoked.

Both initial saturated capacity and the retry needed size are checked against33554432 bytes before resize. Non-Buffer errors and a retry failure propagate; there is no unlimited loop or new general oversized-result recovery promise. This is an encoded-result limit, not a total-process RSS guarantee.
